Then: (1) every simple command must be parsed with certainty, its program word a plain literal (no $, braces, globs, backticks, quotes tricks, no expansion) from an allowlist of programs the root uses (git, gh, echo, printf, cat, head, tail, wc, grep, rg, ls, cd, pwd, mise, bun, bunx, jq, sort, uniq, cut, tr, test, [, true, false, sleep, mkdir, cp, mv, rm, touch, diff, sed, awk, find without -exec/-execdir/-ok/-okdir/-delete... and holyagent wrapper paths); any other program, keyword construct (function, coproc, trap, time with options, source, ., eval, exec, xargs, env with options, shells, subshell with ((, arithmetic with commands) gives unclear; (2) for git, every word is a literal, the subcommand is literal, a commit routes to vcs commit, a push is checked by the existing force rules, and missing subcommand, -c/--config-env overrides of alias, push or remote, or a dynamic word give unclear; (3) git appearing as a non-first word of any command (an argument of another program) gives unclear unless that program only prints text (echo, printf, grep, rg) and the word is quoted data. Keep everyday commands passing with tests: git status/log/show/diff/branch/merge/stash/worktree, plain git push with -u, gh pr create --body-file with a quoted heredoc, gh pr checks --watch, mise run verify piped into tail, bun test, a for loop over literal words calling git log.
Rewrite docs/hooks.md for the allowlist, keeping the documented residuals honest (user git aliases in config files).

Keep only vcs commit (exact paths + Intent state + message check) and vcs pr (PR text check). Intent state stays versioned in Git.
No version-control writes and no edits under .holyagent or the repository metadata folder. Report the changed paths.
